title: ITDCA0-44 Database Design Concepts — Comprehensive Practice Quiz
description: Practice quiz based on the Database Design Concepts topics covered so far: entities, attributes and instances; entity and attribute naming; Barker's notation; UIDs; relationship cardinality and optionality; many-to-many relationships and intersection entities; recursive relationships; hierarchical and network structures; and modelling roles. Questions are for practice and revision.
subject: Database Design Concepts

questions.question: In database modelling, what is an entity?
options: A type of thing or concept about which data is stored
A single value stored in a column
A line connecting two tables only
answer: A type of thing or concept about which data is stored
questions.explanation: An entity represents a type of thing or concept for which the system needs to store information.

questions.question: Which of the following is an instance of the entity PERSON?
In the example PERSON with attributes personID, name and height, which item is an attribute?
Classify each example by matching the object to its correct category.
questions.explanation: PERSON and DOG are entity types, name is an attribute, and Bob Dude is an instance of a suitable person entity.

questions.question: According to the naming convention in the lesson notes, how should an entity name be written?
options: With spaces, for example Employee Name

questions.question: According to the lesson notes, which is the correctly formatted multi-word attribute name?
questions.explanation: The lesson notes specify lowercase attribute names, with each subsequent word starting with a capital letter, such as employeeName.

questions.question: A student should follow the naming conventions specified in the official lesson notes or assessment instructions rather than automatically adopting a convention found online.
In the Barker's notation examples used in the lesson notes, what does # indicate beside an attribute?
In the Barker's notation legend used in the practice material, what does o indicate beside an attribute?
In the Barker's notation legend used in the practice material, what does * indicate beside an attribute?
options: The attribute is a foreign key only
The attribute is an entity name

questions.question: In an ER diagram, attributes should be placed inside the entity soft box according to the practice quiz example.
What is a UID used for in an entity?
options: Uniquely identifying each instance of the entity
Showing that every attribute is optional
answer: Uniquely identifying each instance of the entity

questions.question: Which statements about UIDs are correct? Select all that apply.
options: A UID uniquely identifies an entity instance
A UID may consist of more than one attribute
An intersection entity may use both parent UIDs as a compound UID
A UID is always an entity's descriptive name
answer: A UID uniquely identifies an entity instance
A UID may consist of more than one attribute
An intersection entity may use both parent UIDs as a compound UID

questions.question: A HOTEL has hotelID, address and numParking. Which attribute is the most suitable UID from the options, assuming hotelID is unique?
options: All three must form a compound UID

questions.question: What does a one-to-many relationship between PRODUCT and STOCK mean in the example where STOCK records products held by stores?
options: One PRODUCT can be associated with many STOCK records
One STOCK record must represent many products
Every PRODUCT must have exactly one STOCK record
STOCK and PRODUCT are the same entity
answer: One PRODUCT can be associated with many STOCK records

questions.question: A foreign key relationship to a parent entity automatically means that every parent must have at least one child.
questions.explanation: A parent can have zero children unless the model's rules specify otherwise.

questions.question: A many-to-many relationship exists between PIZZA and FILLING. Which design resolves it in the practice example?
options: Create PIZZA_FILLING as an intersection entity
Place all filling names in one text attribute on PIZZA
Give every pizza the same fillingID
answer: Create PIZZA_FILLING as an intersection entity

questions.question: In the STOCK intersection entity between PRODUCT and STORE, which compound UID is shown in the practice example?
Which statements about the PIZZA–PIZZA_FILLING–FILLING example are correct? Select all that apply.
options: PIZZA_FILLING records which fillings are used on which pizzas
Each PIZZA must have at least one filling in the stated business rules
A PIZZA_FILLING record can refer to a non-existent pizza
answer: PIZZA_FILLING records which fillings are used on which pizzas
Each PIZZA must have at least one filling in the stated business rules

questions.question: What is an intersection entity primarily used for?
options: Resolving a many-to-many relationship into two one-to-many relationships
Replacing all UIDs with descriptive text
Representing only one instance of an entity
answer: Resolving a many-to-many relationship into two one-to-many relationships

questions.question: Arrange the steps for modelling a many-to-many relationship using an intersection entity.
options: Create an intersection entity between them
Carry both parent UIDs into the intersection entity
Define the two relationships between the parents and the intersection entity
answer: Create an intersection entity between them
Carry both parent UIDs into the intersection entity
Define the two relationships between the parents and the intersection entity

questions.question: What is a recursive relationship?
options: A relationship between instances of the same entity type
A relationship that always connects exactly three different entities
A relationship that cannot be represented in SQL
answer: A relationship between instances of the same entity type

questions.question: In the recursive example EMPLOYEE manages EMPLOYEE, what are the two roles played by EMPLOYEE instances?
A recursive relationship means that two separate entity types must always be created, such as MANAGER and EMPLOYEE.
In the SQL implementation of EMPLOYEE manages EMPLOYEE, what does managerID usually reference?
options: employeeID in the same EMPLOYEE table
A separate MANAGER table in every design
answer: employeeID in the same EMPLOYEE table

questions.question: Why might managerID be optional in the EMPLOYEE example?
options: A top-level employee may not have a manager
The EMPLOYEE entity has no attributes
answer: A top-level employee may not have a manager

questions.question: What is the key distinction between a hierarchical recursive structure and a network recursive structure in the lesson example?
options: In a hierarchy each child has at most one parent; in a network a child may have multiple parents
A hierarchy has no entities; a network has no attributes
A network always has exactly two records
answer: In a hierarchy each child has at most one parent; in a network a child may have multiple parents

questions.question: Which example best represents a hierarchy?
options: PIZZA and FILLING connected through PIZZA_FILLING

questions.question: In a network structure where a PART may contain other PARTs, what does CONSTRUCTION_DETAIL represent?
options: An intersection entity recording parent-part/component-part relationships
A new name for the PART UID
A type of attribute naming convention
answer: An intersection entity recording parent-part/component-part relationships

questions.question: In a recursive network structure, why might both parentPartID and componentPartID reference PART?
options: They identify two different roles played by instances of the same entity type
They must have the same value
One is always an attribute of COMPANY
The PART entity has no UID
answer: They identify two different roles played by instances of the same entity type

questions.question: What does modelling roles help a designer do?
options: Describe the different parts or responsibilities played by entities in a relationship
Remove all relationships from the ERD
Turn every entity into an attribute
answer: Describe the different parts or responsibilities played by entities in a relationship

questions.question: In a MOTOR_SERVICE example, the same PERSON entity is referenced as customer and mechanic. What does this demonstrate?
options: One entity type can participate in different roles in a relationship
CUSTOMER and MECHANIC must always be attributes
Roles remove the need for foreign keys
answer: One entity type can participate in different roles in a relationship

questions.question: Match each concept to its description.
options: Connects instances of the same entity type
answer: Connects instances of the same entity type

questions.question: A hotel model includes GUEST, HOTEL and ROOM. Which attribute is most suitable for ROOM from the list below?
In the hotel example, which attribute most naturally belongs to HOTEL?
In the hotel example, which attribute most naturally belongs to GUEST?
Which attributes from the hotel example are most naturally associated with HOTEL? Select all that apply.
A student draws attributes outside the entity box in a Barker ERD. What should the student do according to the practice quiz convention?
options: Place the attributes inside the entity soft box
Move all attributes to a separate page
Turn every attribute into a relationship
answer: Place the attributes inside the entity soft box

questions.question: If a source outside the module uses a different naming style, that automatically overrides the naming convention stated in the official lesson notes.
Arrange these levels from the broadest parent level to the most specific child level in the hierarchy example.
Which checks are useful when reviewing an ERD? Select all that apply.
options: Check that each entity has an appropriate UID
Check that attributes belong to the correct entity
Check relationship cardinality and optionality against the scenario
Use any naming convention regardless of the lesson notes
Check whether a many-to-many relationship needs an intersection entity
answer: Check that each entity has an appropriate UID
Check that attributes belong to the correct entity
Check relationship cardinality and optionality against the scenario
Check whether a many-to-many relationship needs an intersection entity
